title: Understanding Compression Tap Leaks: The Worn Washer
description: An educational breakdown explaining how a degraded rubber washer causes continuous dripping from a traditional compression tap spout.
image_prompt: A detailed vertical 9:16 educational cutaway technical illustration of a brass compression tap valve stem inside a clean chrome faucet body. The cross-section clearly reveals the internal mechanism: a threaded brass stem and an aged black rubber washer with visible flattened edges and small cracks, resting against an internal brass valve seat. A single clear drop of water is shown slowly seeping past the damaged rubber seal down toward the spout channel. Professional neutral lighting with soft studio contrast focused sharply on the central valve assembly. Adequate clear visual space provided at the top third and bottom third of the vertical frame. High technical detail, realistic metal and rubber textures, realistic geometry. Strictly no text, no labels, no diagrams, no arrows, no watermarks, no logos.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear cutaway view of a compression tap to show what happens inside the valve body when a tap is turned off. Viewers can see the exact interaction between the internal brass seat and the black rubber washer. By displaying tiny cracks and deformation on the washer alongside a droplet bypassing the seal, the visual demonstrates why tightening the handle harder will not stop the leak and actually accelerates seal damage.

on_image_text.hook: Why Does Your Tap Keep Dripping?
on_image_text.explanation: A deformed or cracked rubber washer fails to form a complete water barrier against the valve seat.
on_image_text.takeaway: Replace damaged soft seals promptly to protect the brass valve seat from water scoring.
